title.zh: 中国人的精神：科学家与建设者

clips.send: 1964. Yuan Longping. Yuan finds a male-sterile rice plant.
clips.text: 1964. Yuan Longping. Yuan finds a male-sterile rice plant.

clips.send: 1971. Tu Youyou. A sweet wormwood extract works against malaria parasites in an animal test.
clips.text: 1971. Tu Youyou. A sweet wormwood extract works against malaria parasites in an animal test.

clips.send: 1972. Tu Youyou. Tu’s team isolates the compound later named artemisinin.
clips.text: 1972. Tu Youyou. Tu’s team isolates the compound later named artemisinin.

clips.send: Chien-Shiung Wu. Wu grew up in China and worked as a physicist in the U.S. She and her collaborators showed that one kind of radioactive decay behaves differently from its mirror image. They cooled cobalt-60 and used a magnetic field to line up its nuclear spins. More electrons came out in the direction opposite to the spins.
clips.text: Chien-Shiung Wu. Wu grew up in China and worked as a physicist in the U.S. She and her collaborators showed that one kind of radioactive decay behaves differently from its mirror image. They cooled cobalt-60 and used a magnetic field to line up its nuclear spins. More electrons came out in the direction opposite to the spins.

clips.send: Tu Youyou. Tu led a team that discovered artemisinin, a compound used to treat malaria. She received half of the 2015 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. A fourth-century medical text by Ge Hong described soaking sweet wormwood. That gave Tu’s team an idea: try extracting substances from the plant at a lower temperature.

clips.send: 1957. Chien-Shiung Wu. Wu and her collaborators publish their experimental results.
clips.text: 1957. Chien-Shiung Wu. Wu and her collaborators publish their experimental results.

clips.send: 1960. Red Flag Canal workers. Work begins on the Red Flag Canal in Lin County.
clips.text: 1960. Red Flag Canal workers. Work begins on the Red Flag Canal in Lin County.

clips.send: Yuan Longping. Yuan and other researchers bred high-yield hybrid rice by crossing different lines of rice. In 1964, he examined clusters of rice flowers with a magnifying glass. He found a male-sterile plant. It made no pollen that could fertilize an egg, but pollen from another line could help it set seed.

clips.send: 1969. Red Flag Canal workers. The full Red Flag Canal network, including its branch channels, is completed.

clips.send: Qian Xuesen. Qian worked with Caltech’s early rocketry team and later helped build China’s rocket and space programs. U.S. authorities barred him from leaving for several years. Once the ban was lifted in 1955, he and his family left Los Angeles by ship for China.

clips.send: 1965. Red Flag Canal workers. Water begins flowing through the Red Flag Canal’s main channel.
clips.text: 1965. Red Flag Canal workers. Water begins flowing through the Red Flag Canal’s main channel.

clips.send: Zhan Tianyou. Zhan led construction of the railway from Beijing to Zhangjiakou. It opened in 1909. At Qinglongqiao, he laid out a switchback. Trains could take a longer route up the mountain by reversing direction on the tracks.

clips.send: Deng Jiaxian. Deng led teams in China’s early nuclear weapons program. Yang Zhenning later wrote about him in the essay “Deng Jiaxian.” In 1958 he took on classified work. He could no longer tell even his family where he was going for work.

clips.send: 1955. Qian Xuesen. After the U.S. travel ban is lifted, Qian returns to China.

clips.send: 1930. Wen Yiduo. Wen takes a teaching post in Qingdao, where he studies Tang poetry.
clips.text: 1930. Wen Yiduo. Wen takes a teaching post in Qingdao, where he studies Tang poetry.

clips.send: Wen Yiduo. Wen wrote poetry and studied classical Chinese literature. He was also a public speaker in the democracy movement. Zang Kejia, his student in Qingdao, remembered Wen’s cluttered desk from the years when Wen was studying Tang poetry.

clips.send: 1929. Lin Qiaozhi. Lin graduates and joins the staff at Peking Union Medical College Hospital.
clips.text: 1929. Lin Qiaozhi. Lin graduates and joins the staff at Peking Union Medical College Hospital.

clips.send: Lin Qiaozhi. Lin cared for mothers and newborns and helped develop medical care for women in China. In the 1950s, she sent staff to the Soviet Union to learn how to examine cells for signs of disease. After they returned, her team began screening for cervical cancer.

clips.send: Red Flag Canal workers. People in Lin County, Henan, built the canal to bring water from the Zhuozhang River to communities short of water. The canal museum describes how one woman could hold two steel chisels, one in each hand, while others struck them with hammers to cut the rock.

clips.send: 袁隆平。袁隆平和其他科研人员让不同品系的水稻杂交，培育出高产的杂交水稻。1964年，他拿着放大镜观察稻穗，找到一株雄性不育的水稻。这株水稻的花粉不能完成受精，用另一个品系的花粉授粉后却可以结籽。

clips.send: 吴健雄。吴健雄在中国长大，后来在美国从事物理研究。她和合作者发现，有一种放射性衰变在镜像条件下会表现出不同的结果。他们将钴-60冷却到极低温度，用磁场使原子核的自旋方向趋于一致。结果发现，沿自旋相反方向飞出的电子更多。

clips.send: 邓稼先。邓稼先在中国早期核武器研制中承担了科研领导工作。杨振宁后来写了《邓稼先》一文。1958年，他开始从事保密工作，连自己的去向也不能告诉家人。

clips.send: 1971年，屠呦呦。青蒿提取物在动物实验中显示出抗疟效果。

clips.send: 屠呦呦。屠呦呦带领团队发现了可用于治疗疟疾的青蒿素。她获得了2015年诺贝尔生理学或医学奖的一半份额。公元4世纪葛洪的医书记载了浸泡青蒿的方法。这启发屠呦呦团队尝试在较低温度下提取青蒿中的成分。

clips.send: 詹天佑。詹天佑主持修建京张铁路。这条铁路于1909年通车。在青龙桥，他设计了“人”字形线路。列车折返后继续上山，走更长的路来降低坡度。

clips.send: 1960年，红旗渠建设者。林县开始修建红旗渠。
clips.text: 1960年，红旗渠建设者。林县开始修建红旗渠。

clips.send: 红旗渠建设者。河南林县缺水，当地群众修建红旗渠，把浊漳河的水引进林县。红旗渠纪念馆介绍过一种凿石分工：一名女工两手各扶一根钢钎，其他工人用锤敲击钢钎。

clips.send: 1969年，红旗渠建设者。包括各级支渠在内的红旗渠全线工程建成。
clips.text: 1969年，红旗渠建设者。包括各级支渠在内的红旗渠全线工程建成。

clips.send: 林巧稚。林巧稚为产妇和新生儿诊治，推动了中国妇产科医疗的发展。20世纪50年代，她派医务人员到苏联学习怎样通过检查细胞发现病变。进修人员回国后，她的团队开展了宫颈癌筛查。

clips.send: 闻一多。闻一多写新诗、研究中国古典文学，也在民主运动中公开演讲。闻一多在青岛钻研唐诗。学生臧克家回忆起那段日子时，提到了闻一多凌乱的书桌。

clips.send: 1965年，红旗渠建设者。红旗渠总干渠开始通水。

clips.send: 钱学森。钱学森参与加州理工学院早期的火箭研究，后来参与创建中国的火箭和航天事业。美国当局曾多年不准钱学森离境。1955年禁令解除后，他和家人从洛杉矶乘船回国。
